```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# import files:
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

electricity_generation_by_source <- read_csv("electricity-generation-by-source.csv")
economic_damage_from_natural_disasters_wind <- read_csv("economic-damage-from-natural-disasters.csv")
```

## Data cleanup

here we clean up the electrricity generation data:

```{r plot-data}
# import files:
# View(electricity_generation_by_source |> filter(Entity == "World"))
plotdata <- 
  electricity_generation_by_source |> 
  filter(Entity == "World") |>
  full_join(economic_damage_from_natural_disasters |> filter(Entity == "Extreme weather"), join_by(Year))
  
  #View()
```


```{r plot-test 1}

# 2. Create the scatter plot
plot(plotdata$Year, plotdata$Wind,
     xlab = "Year", ylab = "Energy generated by source. wind")
```

```{r plot-test2}
# 1. Transform ONLY Wind into log10 space (+1 handles zeroes safely)
plotdata_log <- plotdata %>%
  mutate(log_Wind = log10(Wind + 1))

# 2. Calculate the scaling factor between linear damages and log wind
max_log_energy <- max(plotdata_log$log_Wind, na.rm = TRUE) *2
max_linear_damages <- max(plotdata_log$`Total economic damages`, na.rm = TRUE)
scale_factor <- max_linear_damages / max_log_energy

# 3. Generate the plot starting from 1975
ggplot(plotdata_log, aes(x = Year)) +
  # Primary Axis: Log-transformed Wind Energy
  geom_line(aes(y = log_Wind, color = "Wind Energy"), linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Secondary Axis: Linear Damages scaled down to fit the log axis range
  geom_line(aes(y = `Total economic damages` / scale_factor, color = "Damages (USD)"), linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Configure the hybrid Log-Linear Y-Axes
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Wind Energy (Log Scale)",
    # Reverts log numbers (1, 2, 3) back to readable values (10, 100, 1000)
    labels = function(x) scales::comma(10^x),
    
    # Secondary axis reverses the linear division to display the original dollar values
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . * scale_factor, 
      name = "Total Economic Damages (USD, Linear Scale)", 
      labels = scales::dollar
    )
  ) +
  
  # Set the X-axis timeline constraints starting in 1975
  # Note: If your Year column is a Date class, use: c(as.Date("1975-01-01"), max(plotdata_log\$Year))
  xlim(1975, max(plotdata_log$Year, na.rm = TRUE)) +
  
  # Styling and Legends
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Wind Energy" = "blue", "Damages (USD)" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Wind Energy (Log) and Economic Damages (Linear) Over Time",
    x = "Year",
    color = "Legend"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
